title: Aristotle lists seven sources of apparent refutation that do not depend on language
summary: Aristotle lists seven sources of apparent refutation that do not depend on language.
body: Outside language, the translation says, there are seven kinds: accident; using an expression absolutely or with a qualification of respect, place, time, or relation; ignorance of what a refutation is; the consequent; assuming the original point; stating as cause what is not a cause; and making several questions into one. The source says: "Of fallacies, on the other hand, that are independent of language there are seven kinds: (1) that which depends upon Accident: (2) the use of an expression absolutely or not absolutely but with some qualification of respect or place, or time, or relation: (3) that which depends upon ignorance of what 'refutation' is: (4) that which depends upon the consequent: (5) that which depends upon assuming the original conclusion: (6" The list is Aristotle's, in this translation. A modern textbook name for one of these patterns is not a license to treat the label as a proof that a speaker is wrong about the substance.
